clue.text: One particular exercise poet doesn't finish

indicators.note: a word that fails to finish stops short, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
Dante Alighieri, the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A writer who never quite completes a particular workout.
explanation.walkthrough: PE plus DANT(e) gives PEDANT. 'Particular' here is an adjective meaning fussy, not 'specific'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedant is a fussy person who insists on precise detail, so 'one particular' in the sense of finicky describes them.

clue.text: Injection of wit over island language

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing over another is written above it, so the parts stack in that order

blocks.note: a pun is a piece of verbal wit
a jab is an informal word for an injection
I is the standard abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A dose of humour administered to the language spoken on some island.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'injection of wit' as wit's injection: PUN then JAB, sitting over I to give PUNJABI.
explanation.definitionFit: Punjabi is the tongue spoken in the Punjab region of India and Pakistan, an example of a language.

clue.text: Appreciate model not having small figure

indicators.note: something not having a part lacks it, so that part is taken away

blocks.note: to dig something is slang for liking or appreciating it
to sit for a painter is to model for them
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Admiring a model who lacks a small figure, as if she were slim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small figure' looks like a phrase about a slim model; it splits into S, which leaves SIT, and the definition 'figure'.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit is a single numeral from nought to nine, which is one sense of the word figure.

clue.text: Ignore heart on cuckoo's wings — impossible!

indicators.note: the heart of something is its centre, so only the middle letters are kept
wings sit at either side of a body, so only the outside letters are kept
a word placed on the wings sits between them, so it goes inside the pair

blocks.note: the two central letters of the six-letter word
the first and last letters of the bird's name
on can mean plus or in addition, as does and

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry that disregarding a cuckoo is out of the question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' does double service as a plus sign: it means 'and', which sits between the bird's outer letters. The answer is a pidgin-style phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: No can do is a colloquial way of saying a request cannot be carried out, an exclamation meaning it is not possible.

clue.text: Underwear found in shops aboard ship

indicators.note: goods aboard a vessel are carried inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a mall is a shopping centre full of shops
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Knickers turn up in the boutiques on a cruise liner.
explanation.walkthrough: SS for steamship is a standard abbreviation. 'Smalls' is a British informal word for underwear, often heard of washing on a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Smalls is a British colloquial term for underclothes such as pants and knickers, so it is a synonym for underwear.

clue.text: Demote oldest pastor, essentially for being shy

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so each word gives up only its central letters

blocks.note: the two central letters of the six-letter verb
the two central letters of the six-letter adjective
the two central letters of the six-letter noun

explanation.surface: A church's senior minister is moved down the ranks because of timidity.
explanation.walkthrough: Each of the three six-letter words gives its middle pair: MO, DE and ST make MODEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Modest and shy are close synonyms, both describing a retiring person who avoids drawing attention to themselves.

clue.text: One who disappeared in grinding lunar cold

indicators.note: grinding breaks material up and mixes it, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: the nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An astronaut lost forever in the bitter cold of the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Lucan was a British earl who vanished in 1974 after his children's nanny was murdered, and was never found.
explanation.definitionFit: The earl famously went missing without trace, and his fate remains one of Britain's best-known unsolved mysteries.

clue.text: Photographed piece that can encourage reluctant union

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the noun

blocks.note: a photographed scene has been shot
piece is slang for a firearm

explanation.surface: A snapshot of a weapon that pushes an unwilling couple to the altar.
explanation.walkthrough: A shotgun wedding is one forced on a couple, traditionally by the bride's father threatening the groom, often because of a pregnancy.
explanation.definitionFit: The firearm is what, in the old joke, persuades a hesitant groom into marriage, hence the shotgun wedding idiom.

clue.text: World War One is grotesque whatever the outcome

indicators.note: something grotesque is distorted out of its natural shape, so these letters are reshaped

blocks.note: all thirteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A judgment that the Great War was hideous, however it ended.
explanation.walkthrough: The war's name looks like the subject, but every one of its letters, plus 'is', is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Win, lose or draw covers every possible result of a contest, so it means regardless of how things turn out.

clue.text: Problem amalgamating tin and silver

indicators.note: amalgamating combines things into one, so the two symbols are joined together

blocks.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A metallurgist hits trouble when trying to alloy two metals.
explanation.walkthrough: Chemical symbols are a common crossword source: SN for tin from Latin stannum, AG for silver from argentum.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is an unexpected obstacle or drawback, a straightforward synonym for a difficulty.

clue.text: Rich old fop contrived to keep kids out

definitions.note: a purpose phrase standing for the adjective, designed to keep children out

indicators.note: something contrived is artificially arranged, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: all ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A wealthy elderly dandy schemes to bar children from his house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contrived' reads as the fop's scheming verb, but it signals the rearrangement of his own description.
explanation.definitionFit: Childproof describes locks, caps or rooms built so that young children cannot get into them or tamper with them.

clue.text: Press lecturer to leave stuff

indicators.note: when someone leaves they are no longer present, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: to press something is to squash it flat
L is the standard abbreviation for lecturer

explanation.surface: Journalists urge an academic to abandon his belongings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like the newspapers and 'stuff' like possessions; both are verbs. FLATTEN without L gives FATTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff a goose or a person is to feed them heavily, making them plumper, which is a synonym in the verb sense.

clue.text: Survive stages on them? You're nearly finished!

definitions.note: the phrase completes as 'on your last legs'

blocks.note: to last is to endure or survive
legs are stages of a journey or race

explanation.surface: Advice to a flagging runner to get through the final stages before collapsing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a fill-in: 'on them' points to the idiom 'on your last legs', so the answer is what 'them' refers to.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on one's last legs is an idiom for being exhausted or close to collapse or death, i.e. almost done for.

clue.text: Off heroin? On it, you are quite arrogant

definitions.text: On it, you are quite arrogant
definitions.note: a fill-in for the idiom 'on your high horse'

blocks.note: meat that has gone off is said to be high
horse is old slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Someone who has quit drugs is told they are being rather full of themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off heroin' suggests having kicked the habit, but 'off' means rotten, i.e. HIGH, and heroin is HORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on your high horse is an idiom for behaving in a superior, self-righteous or haughty manner.

clue.text: It contains holy text that choristers share in harmony

definitions.text: It contains holy text that choristers share in harmony

blocks.note: surface reading: some religious document or book
setter's reading: the idiom about everyone singing from the same page, meaning being in agreement

explanation.surface: A page of sacred words passed among a choir as they sing together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In harmony' is both musical and the idiom 'singing from the same hymn sheet', meaning agreeing on a common message.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymn sheet is a printed page of the words of religious songs, which a choir reads from while singing in unison.

clue.text: Hustler's confession displayed on computer

definitions.note: a participial phrase standing for the noun, a thing shown on screen

blocks.note: a confession is made in the first person, opening with the speaker's own pronoun
a hustler's stock in trade is a swindle, and what he owns up to is that he does it

explanation.surface: A fraudster's admission appears on a screen.
explanation.walkthrough: A hustler admitting his trade would say 'I con', which runs together as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is the small clickable picture on a desktop or phone screen representing a program or file.

clue.text: This employee makes pittance at first

definitions.text: This employee makes pittance at first

indicators.note: what comes at first is the opening, so each word gives up only its leading letter

blocks.note: the leading letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A worker grumbles that this staff member started on poverty wages.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the initials spell the worker, and the sentence describes one.
explanation.definitionFit: A temp is a temporary office worker, often low-paid at the start of an assignment, hence the description as a poorly paid employee.

clue.text: Ambassador involved in crash may have a grievance

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be caught up within it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: a thump is a heavy crashing blow or noise
HE is His Excellency, the form of address for an ambassador

explanation.surface: A diplomat caught up in a car accident is likely to be aggrieved.
explanation.walkthrough: His Excellency is the formal address for an ambassador. 'Having the hump' is British slang for being sulky or annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: The hump is British slang for a fit of resentment or sulking, so it means a sense of being wronged.

clue.text: Support rigid line, for example

blocks.note: wooden means stiff or rigid in manner
a leg of a triangle is one of its lines

explanation.surface: Backing a strict policy, offered as an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For example' belongs with 'Support': a wooden leg is one kind of support, so the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden leg is a prosthesis that bears a person's weight, an example of something that holds them up.

clue.text: One coming out demanding dismissal of fellow composer

indicators.note: dismissal sends someone away, so that letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: a deb, or debutante, is a young woman coming out into society
a fussy person is demanding and hard to please
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A débutante insists that a colleague of a musician be sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow composer' reads as a colleague; 'fellow' is the letter dropped and 'composer' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Debussy was the French Impressionist who wrote Clair de lune and La Mer, an example of a composer.

clue.text: Conspicuous coverage of competition by papers? Just the opposite

indicators.note: to cover something is to wrap around it, so one piece goes around another
this flips who covers whom in the order the surface states

blocks.note: an event is a sporting competition
ID papers are identity documents

explanation.surface: Splashy newspaper reporting of a contest, though in fact it is the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: As written the papers cover the contest; 'just the opposite' turns that round so the competition holds the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Evident means plainly visible or obvious, a direct synonym of conspicuous.

clue.text: Under pressure, debate moving queen up one space — capital!

indicators.note: in a down clue what lies under comes below, so the rest follows the first letter
moving shifts a letter's place, so the order of the word is changed
in a down entry up means earlier, so the letter shifts one slot towards the start

blocks.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
to debate is to argue
names the letter that moves, R for Regina; it adds no letters of its own

explanation.surface: A chess game under stress, advancing the queen a square, earns a cry of 'Excellent!'
explanation.walkthrough: Queen is R (Regina). In ARGUE the R moves up one place in this down entry, giving RAGUE under P.
explanation.definitionFit: Prague is the capital city of the Czech Republic, so it is an example of a capital.

clue.text: Controlled setter, confident when dismissing second son

indicators.note: dismissing someone sends them away, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself as me
assured means self-confident
S is the abbreviation for second
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A composed puzzle-maker, sure of themselves, after firing their younger boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second son' reads as a younger child, but only one S goes: 'second' is a selector, removing the second S of ASSURED.
explanation.definitionFit: A measured response is deliberate and restrained, so the word is a synonym of controlled in that sense.

clue.text: Scientist is away during scrap

indicators.note: during means within a span of time, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: to bin something is to scrap it
to be off is to be away

explanation.surface: A researcher is absent while a fight breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a fight but it is the verb to discard. Boffin is British slang for a scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Boffin is informal British slang for a scientist or technical expert, especially one doing research.

clue.text: Fruit sown occasionally in oriental bed

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: Seeds planted here and there in a garden bed in the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed' plays on the garden sense with fruit sown; here it is somewhere to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A futon is a Japanese padded mattress laid on the floor for sleeping, so it is an Eastern sleeping mat.

clue.text: If you break sugar press, he will tell on you

indicators.note: breaking something smashes it apart, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: all ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Damage the factory machine and the foreman will report you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supergrass' is British slang for an informer who gives evidence against many associates; a grass tells the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A supergrass is a criminal who informs on many accomplices, so the whole phrase describes someone who will betray you.

clue.text: General group heads for The Hague every year

indicators.note: the head of something is its top, so only the leading letters are kept

blocks.note: the leading letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A senior officer's unit travels to the Netherlands annually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like a military rank; it means 'people in general', as in 'they say'.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun is used for people at large or unspecified authorities, as in 'they say it will rain'.

clue.text: Father has time for idle talk

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: pater is Latin, and old public-school slang, for father
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Dad finds a moment to chat about nothing much.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes inside PATER after the second letter; either T of PATTER works.
explanation.definitionFit: Patter is rapid glib chatter, like a salesman's or comedian's, so it is light inconsequential speech.

clue.text: Extremely canny gentlemen edit what's produced by pen

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so each word gives only its outermost letters

blocks.note: first and last letters
first and last letters
first and last letters

explanation.surface: Very shrewd men revise what a writer turns out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' suggests writing; a pen is a female swan. 'Extremely' applies to all three following words.
explanation.definitionFit: A cygnet is a young swan, the offspring hatched by a female swan, which is called a pen.
